description: Machine-readable manifest proving every v1.0 intent has executable proof. A gap here is a gap in the release.

contracts.name: Provider independence
contracts.intent: Core (rules, analysis, report) must not import provider-specific code (nx, moon, native).

evidence.assertion: SHIPPED_PACKAGES allow-list prevents unapproved dependencies; no provider import found in core layers
Only commands/context.mjs imports providers — the designated orchestration layer

contracts.name: Empty result is never silently successful
contracts.intent: An empty diagnostic list must mean 'no violation', and nothing else. Every path that cannot reach a verdict must say so.

evidence.assertion: JSON envelope throws on status=ok + incomplete coverage, status/exitCode disagreement, coverage.complete/notAnalyzed disagreement
analyzed:false on every non-verdict path; empty diagnostic list only from two named places
Exit codes 0/1/3 distinguish clean/findings/cannot-look

contracts.name: Workspace resolution ≠ source analysis
contracts.intent: Graph edges (from provider) and source analysis (from analyzers) answer different questions. Neither replaces the other.

evidence.assertion: Analysis record is a superset of a graph edge — 5 of 15 violations decided on raw specifier
src/graph/ is a lossy view of analysis, on purpose; src/analysis/ never judges

contracts.name: Architecture snapshot identity
contracts.intent: Two runs over an unchanged tree produce byte-identical JSON. Internal fields are stripped. Schema is versioned.

evidence.assertion: Graph, check, impact run twice — byte-identical JSON output
Plain string comparison, never localeCompare; INTERNAL_DATA_FIELDS stripped; SCHEMA_VERSION = 2
computePolicyFingerprint produces SHA-256 of canonicalized policy

contracts.name: Snapshot compatibility
contracts.intent: diff refuses a baseline with unknown schemaVersion. A consumer that reads a schemaVersion it does not recognise should refuse to parse.

evidence.assertion: Invalid baseline schemaVersion exits 3; incompatible version exits 3
parseBaseline validates schemaVersion; refuses unknown versions

contracts.name: Diff semantics — structural ≠ policy ≠ rule-impact
contracts.intent: Graph change ≠ policy impact ≠ violation ≠ drift. Diff separates structural changes, policy mismatch, and rule impact. Refuses incomplete baseline/head.

evidence.assertion: Self-baseline exits 0; added/removed edges reported; policy mismatch warned; rule-impact with config
computeDiff returns structural diff; policyMismatch detected via fingerprint; computeRuleImpact for constraint context

contracts.name: Impact determinism
contracts.intent: Given the same graph and project name, impact always returns the same set. BFS, sorted, no localeCompare.

evidence.assertion: Impact --format json produces identical output on two runs
Sorts results using plain string comparison (never localeCompare)

contracts.name: Context — effective architecture contract
contracts.intent: context shows the constraint table as it applies to a project's tags, not raw metadata. Per-edge verdicts cover depConstraints only — this narrowing is disclosed.

evidence.assertion: Returns tags, matched constraints, per-edge violations; coverage.notes warns about depConstraints-only scope
Native consumer: tags, constraints, coverage.notes verified; Moon consumer: context E2E
Section 'What context and impact do not check' warns agents about the semantic gap

contracts.name: Explain — rule, reason, evidence
contracts.intent: explain runs full evaluate() and returns ALL violations at the site (not just first). Unresolvable sites are explicit, not silent drops.

evidence.assertion: Returns all violations at a site; unresolvable site returns unresolvable:true with reason
Native and Moon consumers: specifier, sourceProject, targetProject, violations verified

contracts.name: Check is enforcement authority
contracts.intent: context/impact/diff/explain must not create different verdicts than check would. The depConstraints-only narrowing in context/impact/diff is disclosed.

evidence.assertion: coverage.notes warns that per-edge verdicts cover only depConstraints
coverage.notes warns that per-edge verdicts cover only depConstraints
Section warns agents: violations:[] means allowed by constraint table, not free of all boundary violations
Test verifies coverage.notes contains depConstraints warning
E2E verifies coverage.notes in JSON envelope

contracts.name: Determinism
contracts.intent: No localeCompare, Date.now, Math.random in production code. Sorts use plain string comparison. Two runs over same tree produce identical output.

evidence.assertion: Graph, check, impact: two runs produce byte-identical JSON
Plain string comparison throughout; never localeCompare

contracts.name: Provider parity
contracts.intent: Same semantics on Nx/Moon/Native: same violation types, same options, same constraint table, same message ids. Partial workspaceLayout rejected.

evidence.assertion: Nx vs Native: project names, edge source/target/type, violation rule IDs, envelope structure
Moon: check, graph, diff, impact, explain, context verified against Moon provider
inferWorkspaceLayout returns null for partial layouts — same all-or-nothing contract as Nx and Native
Partial layout (apps-only, libs-only) returns undefined workspaceLayout

bugsFixed.description: Moon provider returned partial workspaceLayout (e.g., {appsDir:'apps'} with no libsDir), which silently disabled isAbsoluteImportIntoAnotherProject for the missing axis via 'undefined/' string comparison. Fixed: inferWorkspaceLayout returns null for partial layouts, forcing the DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_LAYOUT fallback.

context and impact commands used judgeEdge (depConstraints-only) without disclosing to agents that 11 of 15 violation types were not checked. An agent seeing violations:[] could believe an edge was clean when check would still flag it. Fixed: coverage.notes warns about the narrowing; agentic-development.md documents the gap.

computePolicyFingerprint used raw JSON.stringify without sorting object keys, so two semantically identical policy objects constructed in different key order could produce different fingerprints. diff would then report a spurious policy change. Fixed: canonicalize JSON by sorting keys at every depth before hashing.
